reading.body:
H.R. 7110 is a one-party bill: Summer Lee sponsors it and all sixteen cosponsors are Democrats.

The recorded support is entirely from one side of the aisle, which tells you the bill's path is a messaging path rather than a negotiating one. The issues tagged from its own text are bias and civil rights, so the bill targets how algorithmic systems treat people, not how much compute they consume or where the power comes from. That places it in the governance layer of AI policy, one step removed from the grid and building constraints that set the physical ceiling on scaling.

The data covers sponsorship, cosponsorship, and lobbying mentions. It does not include the bill's text, its committee status, any vote, or any hearing. The lobbying count is the notable absence: zero filings for 2025 or later name the bill. A filing that names a bill only shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken, and here there are none to read either way. So the honest reading is that this is early-stage legislation with unified partisan support and no recorded industry engagement, and nothing in this data says whether it advances.
